title: Monster
author: Walter Dean Myers
current_text: In 2019, Monster was challenged at Gates Middle School (Scituate, MA) for “language, violence, and sexual overtures” and deemed inappropriate for 8th and 9th-graders; after meeting with parents, school administrators removed it from the curriculum, and the ban remained in effect despite protest at a public meeting. After parental complaints about the maturity of language and sexual content in 7th grade reading club selections, a teacher at Signal Mountain (TN) Middle-High School told parents she was removing Monster from the reading list; the principal later said the books were high school reading materials, not 7th grade.

sources.quote:
2019
This New York Times bestselling novel about an incarcerated teen awaiting trial was challenged for “language, violence, and sexual overtures” and deemed inappropriate for 8th and 9th-graders at Gates Middle School (Scituate, MA). After meeting with parents, school administrators decided to remove it from the curriculum. Despite strong protest at a public meeting, the ban remained in effect.
sources.title: Banned Books 2021 – Monster – Marshall University Libraries

sources.quote: After some parental complaints about the maturity of language and sexual content in some 7th grade reading club selections, a teacher at the Signal Mountain (TN) Middle-High School contacted parents to inform them that she was removing All American Boys and Monster from the reading list.
sources.title: Banned Books 2021 – Monster – Marshall University Libraries

sources.quote: In a follow-up statement, the principal indicated that the books were high school reading materials, not 7th grade, and affirmed the school’s commitment to diversity.
